true_answer: In non-relativistic classical mechanics, Newton's concept of 'relative, apparent, and common time' can be used in the formulation of a prescription for the synchronization of clocks. Events seen by two diﬀerent observers in motion relative to each other produce a mathematical concept of time that works suﬃciently well for describing the everyday phenomena of most people's experience. In the late nineteenth century, physicists encountered problems with the classical understanding of time, in connection with the behavior of electricity and magnetism.
